1319	
1320	**Coverage scopes partition, and the two halves of that word have different
1321	owners.** *Disjointness* is the general rule, applies to every relation, and is
1322	**decided at retained Run closure**: two Coverage scopes of one view that share

1328	and is the same tuple `coverageTotality` matches facts on; a Run whose view
1329	violates it refuses with `SUBJECT_SCOPE_PARTITION_OVERLAP` naming the relation,
1330	rung and offending subject. A **differing tuple is a different claim, not an
1331	overlap**, which is why the same subject may lawfully appear under two relations,

1334	Three boundaries of that rule matter and are held by controls. It is **per view**:
1335	two views of one Run may reference the same scope, because a view is one

1338	though they still reach the retained-scope ladder check. And it is decided
1339	**here, not by the producer**: Coverage admission sees one scope and its one
1340	entry, so it cannot decide a property that holds between two scopes; a law nothing
1341	compares is the defect this closes.

1343	Fact totality and the population available for evaluation are separate
1344	obligations. The native relation registry's `coverageTotality` row for
